text.p: Salomon Brothers in a report released on Monday downgraded Tadiran Telecommunications to a hold from a buy and reduced its earnings per share (EPS) estimates for this year and next.
Salomon reduced its 1997 EPS estimate to $1.45 from $1.72 and its sales forecast for 1997 to $487.4 million from $499 million.
For 1998 Salomon lowered its EPS forecast to $1.88 from $2.00 and its sales forecast to $553 million from $584 million.
Salomon said 1997 "remains a year of transition for Tadiran, as it moves from a domestically oriented provider to a global telecom solution player."

Salomon said that although it had expected 1997 to be a transitional year, the weakness in orders was greater than originally anticipated. "Therefore, year to year, 1997 is expected to be an especially weak year for Tadiran."

"We have downgraded Tadiran shares to hold from buy, primarily based on our belief that the stock will trade in the $16-$19 price range for the next few quarters, due to negative quarterly EPS comparisons and a decline in earnings in 1997," the report said.
"In the long term we believe that Tadiran shares will trade substantially higher," the Salomon added.
Tadiran Telecommunications is a subsidiary of Tadiran Ltd.
